originLines: I started building because I was never satisfied with technology being something we simply use — I wanted to understand how it works and imagine what it could become.
What began with curiosity about code gradually turned into a habit of turning ideas into real products, experiments, and interactive experiences.
I became fascinated by the intersection of artificial intelligence, spatial computing, and human interaction — the space where software can feel less like a tool and more like an experience.
Through projects like HoloPad and my other engineering experiments, I have learned that building something ambitious means dealing with uncertainty, failed approaches, and countless iterations.
I am still learning, still experimenting, and still figuring things out. But I would rather build an imperfect version of an idea than spend my life wondering what it could have been.
